leads.summary: Blocking configuration reads can outlast the restart command's fixed IPC readiness budget
leads.consequence: When either config read stalls for longer than the restart script's twenty 0.5-second IPC attempts plus 0.1-second sleeps (nominal maximum around twelve seconds; often less when a negative response is immediate), omarchy-restart-shell exits 1 saying 'Omarchy shell did not become ready after restart.' The newly launched Quickshell may become ready later. No such synchronous config read was imposed on IPC readiness at the merge-base. During the stall lock and other shell IPC targets cannot answer, not just plugin discovery. This is a boundary effect of the proposed startup ordering rather than an argument against loading config first. The new test's 1/3-second delay and direct IPC calls do not exercise this consumer. Consider making restart readiness deadline accommodate blocked config IO and testing its stated result, or otherwise bounding config load failure handling.
leads.triage: corroborated_cost_note; Restart script readiness loop verified by coordinator (bin/omarchy-restart-shell:72-93). Folded into the qualified cost note with Opus hung-storage source analysis; not a separate finding.

leads.summary: An initial failed or incomplete user-config read still allows fallback settings to overwrite the user's file
leads.consequence: A present user shell.json that is empty or temporarily malformed during the synchronous first read, or a file whose read fails, yields the defaults before the registry and IPC start. Later setBarWidget / setPluginEnabled on that running shell clones the fallback and atomically writes it to shell.json, discarding the absent user fields. The change closes the delayed-success race but not this failure path; the latter also existed before the PR. Quickshell reports file errors synchronously and its state data are empty on failed read. Open PRs #13104 and #12992 separately address parts of the invalid/reload path; integration may be preferable to duplicating their changes. To establish a specific permission-denied overwrite, test a writable but unreadable file under a private HOME in review.py, since QSaveFile's permissions handling was not tested here.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; Pre-existing post-startup invalid/truncated reload clobber path; published as related-PR context, labelled source only.

leads.summary: The new startup test cannot detect a broken later user-config reload
leads.consequence: A plausible accidental simplification is deleting userConfigFile.onLoaded as seemingly redundant after adding the explicit loadDefaults call. All three new test cases still obtain the user config at startup through loadDefaults -> applyShellConfig -> userConfigFile.text(), so the existing assertions can pass. But later watchChanges/reloadConfig reads no longer call applyShellConfig, leaving the running shell on stale settings until restart. Add a case that changes a valid user shell.json after initial discovery and asserts listShellConfig reflects it, plus a reload failure case if claiming fallback semantics for later reads. This is a test-fidelity gap, not a claim that the current head has removed its reload handler.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_opus_followup; Opus mutant run review3/20260927T113032Z-5cf219df: removing shell.qml:142 passes all new cases but breaks reloads. Published as Optional test improvement.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change closes the startup window described in #11349. The new test passes on the head and each of its three cases fails on the unmodified base for the reason it states. No regressions were found.

Sandboxed runs with Quickshell 0.3.1 (offscreen, private home and runtime directories, no compositor or D-Bus):

```text
case                         base (each case 2 of 2 runs)           head (4 of 4 runs)
delayed user shell.json      disabled probe service starts once     never starts
delayed default shell.json   disabled probe service starts once     never starts
early setBarWidget IPC edit  file becomes shipped defaults + edit   custom fields kept, edit applied
```

Both halves of the change are needed, and the test catches the loss of either:
- Without the explicit `loadDefaults(defaultsFile.text())` call, the delayed-defaults case fails. `blockLoading` only blocks when something calls `text()`, and nothing else does during creation.
- Without `blockLoading: true`, all three cases fail.

**Verified mechanism (Quickshell 0.3.1 source, confirmed by instrumented logs):** with `blockLoading`, a `FileView.text()` call made before the file has first loaded waits for the in-flight read and emits `loaded`/`loadFailed` before returning. The root component is created synchronously, IPC handlers register only after that (`postReload()`), and the plugin scan result arrives later on the event loop. On the head the order is:

```text
root onCompleted -> defaults loaded -> user config loaded -> onCompleted ends
  -> then, in either order: plugin scan (enabled services start)
                            and IPC edits (which see the user's config)
```

On the base the scan finished first and the disabled service started, then stopped about 1 s later when the delayed file arrived.

**Verified fallback and reload behaviour:** with both files missing the built-in config is used; with invalid user JSON the shipped defaults are used and a warning is logged. After startup, replacing the user file with its reload read delayed 3 s, IPC `ping` still answered in 25 ms and the old config was served until the new one loaded, so reloads stay asynchronous. The existing `bar`, `plugin-auth-boundary` and `plugins` shell tests give the same results on base and head.

**Optional test improvement:** after this change, `userConfigFile.onLoaded` (`shell/shell.qml:142`) is no longer needed at startup, because `applyShellConfig()` reads the user file through the blocking `text()`. It is the only path by which a successful reload of the user file reaches `shellConfig`. In a diagnostic copy with that one line removed, all three new cases still pass, but reloads stop working:

```text
after startup (user file at position: bottom)   head                       line 142 removed
file replaced on disk with left                 shell shows left           stays bottom
omarchy-bar position right                      shell shows right          stays bottom
then a setBarWidget IPC edit                    file keeps right + edit    file written back to bottom
```

No test in `test/shell.d` reloads a changed `shell.json` in a real shell. One more case in `shell-config-startup-test.sh` (replace the user file or call `reloadConfig` after startup, then poll `listShellConfig`) would cover the reload behaviour the PR description says is preserved.

**Note on cost:** startup now waits for the two config reads, which took under a millisecond in the sandbox's in-memory filesystem. From source, a read that stalls (for example on unresponsive network storage) would keep the shell from answering IPC until it completes, so `omarchy-restart-shell` would report "did not become ready" if the stall outlasts its 20 ping attempts (roughly 2 to 12 s). This matches Quickshell's documented use case for `blockLoading` (configuration loaded before windows) and was only exercised as a bounded 3 s delay.

**Related open PRs:** a different path to the same kind of loss remains and is outside this PR. From source (not run): after startup, a reload that reads an empty, truncated or invalid user file falls back to defaults, and the next settings change saves them. #12992, #13104 and #7723 target variants of that path, and each one's `shell.qml` changes apply cleanly on top of this head on their own.
